extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, corporate counsel, investor_relations and compliance officers preparing proxy/consent solicitation and SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for disclosure of executive and director compensation, pay ratio, golden parachute, and pay-versus-performance information in proxy/consent solicitation and annual report filings under Item 402 of Regulation S-K. Includes required tables, narrative disclosures, methodology rules, exemptions, and filing/timing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director compensation — types of compensation required to be disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Such compensation must include, but is not limited to: (A) Perquisites and other personal benefits, or property, unless the aggregate amount of such compensation is less than $10,000; (B) All “gross-ups” or other amounts reimbursed during the fiscal year for the payment of taxes; (C) For any security ... purchased ... at a discount ... the compensation cost, if any, computed in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718; (D) Amount paid or accrued to any director pursuant to a plan or arrangement in connection with resignation, retirement, termination, or a change in control; (E) Contributions or allocations to vested and unvested defined contribution plans; (F) Consulting fees; (G) Annual costs of director legacy programs and similar charitable award programs; (H) Dollar value of insurance premiums paid with respect to life insurance for benefit of a director; (I) Dollar value of any dividends or other earnings paid on stock or option awards when not factored into grant date fair value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes all items listed (A)–(I) when material. For perquisites and personal benefits, the $10,000 de minimis threshold applies. For discounted purchases of securities, compute compensation cost per FASB ASC Topic 718. For director legacy/charitable programs, provide footnote disclosure of total dollar amount payable and other material terms. Individual perquisites should be identified and quantified as required elsewhere (Instruction 4 to Item 402(c)(2)(ix)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charitable awards/director legacy programs disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs in which smaller reporting companies agree to make donations to one or more charitable institutions in a director's name are charitable awards programs or director legacy programs for purposes of disclosure required by paragraph (r)(2)(vii)(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide footnote disclosure of the total dollar amount payable under the program and other material terms of each such program for which tabular disclosure is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping directors in the Director Compensation Table
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more directors may be grouped in a single row in the Table if all elements of their compensation are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The names of the directors for whom disclosure is presented on a group basis should be clear from the Table (i.e., grouping only allowed when all compensation elements identical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative description accompanying director compensation table
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative description of any material factors necessary to an understanding of the director compensation disclosed in this Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material factors will vary; examples include (i) a description of standard compensation arrangements (fees for retainer, committee service, chairman service, meeting attendance), and (ii) whether any director has a different compensation arrangement, identifying that director and describing the terms of that arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-application of Item (n) instructions to director compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions 2 and 4 to paragraph (n) of this Item; the Instructions to paragraphs (n)(2)(iii) and (iv); (n)(2)(v) and (vi); (n)(2)(vii); (n)(2)(viii); (n)(2)(ix); and paragraph (o)(7) apply equally to paragraph (r) of this Item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Instructions apply to the columns in the Director Compensation Table that are analogous to the columns in the Summary Compensation Table and to disclosures under paragraph (r) that correspond to analogous disclosures in paragraph (n). (Use referenced instructions for analogous reporting and quantification rules.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative disclosure of compensation policies/practices as they relate to risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that risks arising from the registrant's compensation policies and practices for its employees are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on the registrant, discuss the registrant's policies and practices of compensating its employees as they relate to risk management practices and risk-taking incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations that may trigger disclosure include: business units with significant portion of risk profile; units with compensation structured significantly differently; units significantly more profitable; units where compensation expense is a large percentage of revenues; or policies that vary significantly from overall registrant risk/reward (e.g., short-term bonuses for long-term-risk tasks). Examples of issues to address: (1) general design philosophy and implementation for affected employees; (2) registrant's risk assessment or incentive considerations in structuring compensation; (3) how policies relate to realization of risks short- and long-term (clawbacks, holding periods); (4) policies regarding adjustments to address changes in risk profile; (5) material adjustments made as a result of changes in risk profile; (6) extent to which registrant monitors policies/practices to determine if risk management objectives are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden parachute compensation — required disclosure in proxy/consent solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: In connection with any proxy or consent solicitation providing Item 14A(b)(1) disclosure or a proxy/consent solicitation that includes Item 14 of Schedule 14A disclosure, with respect to each named executive officer of the acquiring and target company, provide the information specified regarding any agreement or understanding concerning any compensation based on or relating to an acquisition, merger, consolidation, sale or other disposition of all or substantially all assets (golden parachute compensation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure shall be presented in a tabular format labeled "Golden Parachute Compensation" with columns for Name (a), Cash ($) (b), Equity ($) (c), Pension/NQDC ($) (d), Perquisites/benefits ($) (e), Tax reimbursement ($) (f), Other ($) (g), Total ($) (h). Include for each named executive officer; aggregate dollar values and footnotes quantifying separate forms of compensation required (see Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden parachute table — contents for each named executive officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The table shall include for each named executive officer: (i) name; (ii) aggregate dollar value of any cash severance payments (base salary, bonus, pro‑rated non‑equity incentive plan payments); (iii) aggregate dollar value of (A) stock awards for which vesting would be accelerated, (B) in‑the‑money option awards for which vesting would be accelerated, (C) payments in cancellation of stock and option awards; (iv) aggregate dollar value of pension and nonqualified deferred compensation benefit enhancements; (v) aggregate dollar value of perquisites and other personal benefits or property and health care/welfare benefits; (vi) aggregate dollar value of any tax reimbursements; (vii) aggregate dollar value of any other compensation based on/relating to the transaction not reported in columns (b)–(f); (viii) aggregate dollar value of the sum of amounts in columns (b)–(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify each separate form of compensation in footnotes for columns (b)–(g); quantify perquisites and personal benefits individually as required by Instruction 4 to Item 402(c)(2)(ix). Use valuation rules specified (e.g., compute dollar value of in-the-money options by difference between transaction price and exercise price). Include only compensation based on/relating to the subject transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification assumptions — timing and price per share rules for golden parachute disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If disclosure is included in a proxy/consent solicitation seeking approval of an acquisition or in a proxy including Item 14 disclosure, quantify assuming the triggering event took place on the latest practicable date and determine price per share as: (a) fixed dollar amount if shareholders receive fixed dollar amount; or (b) average closing market price over first five business days following first public announcement if value not fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute dollar value of in-the-money option awards as the difference between this price and the exercise/base price. Include only compensation that is based on or otherwise relates to the subject transaction. Apply Instruction 1 to Item 402(t) with respect to executive officers required to be disclosed in the issuer's most recent filing that required Item 402(c) disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden parachute disclosure — alternative quantification for annual meeting proxy solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If disclosure is in a proxy solicitation for the annual meeting for purposes of subjecting agreements to a shareholder vote, quantify assuming triggering event took place on the last business day of the registrant's last completed fiscal year and use the closing market price as of that date to determine per‑share value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute dollar value of in-the-money option awards as difference between that price and exercise/base price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable estimates and material assumptions when uncertainties exist in golden parachute amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: If uncertainties exist as to the provision of payments and benefits or the amounts involved, the registrant must make a reasonable estimate applicable to the payment or benefit and disclose material assumptions underlying such estimates. Such disclosure may require forward‑looking information as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making estimates disclose material assumptions; quantify in footnotes where appropriate; include forward-looking info if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote quantification and double-/single-trigger distinctions in golden parachute disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of columns (b) through (g), include a footnote quantifying each separate form of compensation included in the aggregate total. For purposes of quantifying health care benefits, use assumptions used for financial reporting under GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each column (b)–(h), include a footnote quantifying the amount payable attributable to double‑trigger arrangements (amounts triggered by change‑in‑control conditioned upon termination without cause or resignation for good reason within limited timeframe) specifying timeframe, and amount payable attributable to single‑trigger arrangements (amounts triggered by change‑in‑control not conditioned on termination/resignation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate tables when shareholder advisory votes cover both old and new arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant conducting a shareholder advisory vote to cover new arrangements and/or revised terms and previously voted arrangements must provide two separate tables: (1) disclose all golden parachute compensation including previously disclosed arrangements and new/revised terms, and (2) disclose only the new arrangements and/or revised terms subject to the separate shareholder vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clarity about which arrangements are included in each table and avoid mixing scopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification when disclosure involves acquiring company arrangements and separate shareholder advisory votes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Item 402(t)(2) requires disclosure of arrangements between an acquiring company and named executives of the soliciting target company, the registrant shall clarify whether these agreements are included in the separate shareholder advisory vote under §240.14a-21(c) by providing a separate table of all agreements subject to that vote if different from full scope of golden parachute compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear labeling and separate tables as necessary to show which agreements are subject to which shareholder advisory votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative description of material factors for contracts and payments in golden parachute disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a succinct narrative description of any material factors necessary to an understanding of each such contract, agreement, plan or arrangement and the payments quantified in the tabular disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors shall include, but not be limited to: (i) the specific circumstances that would trigger payment(s); (ii) whether payments would be lump sum or annual (disclose duration and by whom provided); (iii) any material conditions or obligations applicable to receipt of payment or benefits, including non‑compete, non‑solicit, non‑disparagement or confidentiality agreements, including duration and waiver/breach provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/applicability of Item 402(t) by registrant type
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that does not qualify as a 'smaller reporting company' must provide information required by Item 402(t) with respect to individuals covered by Items 402(a)(3)(i)–(iii). A registrant that qualifies as a 'smaller reporting company' must provide Item 402(t) information with respect to individuals covered by Items 402(m)(2)(i) and (ii). The obligation does not apply to agreements with senior management of foreign private issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which named executive officers are within scope based on registrant status (smaller reporting company, foreign private issuer exceptions) and apply disclosure only for those individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay ratio disclosure — required items
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose: (i) The median of the annual total compensation of all employees of the registrant, except the PEO; (ii) The annual total compensation of the PEO; (iii) The ratio of the amount in (i) to the amount in (ii) (the ratio may be expressed as 1 to X or narratively as the multiple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the ratio, the amount in (i) shall equal one, or alternatively present as multiple. Provide the three items for the registrant's last completed fiscal year as required in filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay ratio — definitions of total compensation, annual total compensation, and registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of pay ratio: (i) Total compensation for the median of annual total compensation and the PEO shall be determined in accordance with paragraph (c)(2)(x) of this Item (with references to 'named executive officer' deemed to refer to 'employee'); (ii) Annual total compensation means total compensation for registrant's last completed fiscal year; (iii) Registrant means the registrant and its consolidated subsidiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-salaried employees, references to 'base salary' may be deemed to refer to 'wages plus overtime' where applicable. Ensure consistency with Summary Compensation Table rules when adapting to employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of employee for pay ratio purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Employee or employee of the registrant means an individual employed by the registrant or any of its consolidated subsidiaries, whether full‑time, part‑time, seasonal, or temporary, as of a date chosen within the last three months of the last completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes workers employed and compensated by an unaffiliated third party (independent contractors or 'leased' workers). The chosen date must be within the last three months of the fiscal year and disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions of non‑U.S. employees from pay ratio — data privacy and de minimis exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A non‑U.S. employee may be exempt from the definition of employee for pay ratio if: (i) the employee is in a foreign jurisdiction where laws/regulations governing data privacy make obtaining/processing necessary information for compliance unlawful despite reasonable efforts (data privacy exemption); or (ii) the registrant's non‑U.S. employees account for 5% or less of total employees (de minimis exemption), subject to particular rules about jurisdictional exclusions and aggregation with the data privacy exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using data privacy exemption, list excluded jurisdictions, identify specific law/regulation, explain how compliance would violate it (including efforts made to obtain/process info or seek exemptions), provide approximate number of employees exempted per jurisdiction, and file a legal opinion from counsel as an exhibit. If using de minimis exemption, disclose jurisdictions excluded, approximate numbers excluded per jurisdiction, total number of employees irrespective of exemptions, and total number used in de minimis calculation. Registrant may combine exemptions subject to aggregation limits; if data privacy exclusions reach or exceed 5% cannot use de minimis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose date chosen for identifying the median employee
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant shall disclose the date within the last three months of its last completed fiscal year that it selected to identify its median employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the registrant changes the date from the prior year, disclose the change and provide a brief explanation for the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for identifying the median employee — triennial identification and re-identification
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant is required to identify its median employee only once every three years and calculate total compensation for that employee each year, provided there has been no change in employee population or compensation arrangements that the registrant reasonably believes would result in a significant change to pay ratio disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no significant changes, disclose using the same median employee and briefly state basis for reasonable belief. If there has been a change reasonably believed to significantly affect the pay ratio, re-identify the median employee for that year. If the original median employee's circumstances change such that they no longer are appropriate, registrant may use another employee whose compensation is substantially similar to the original median employee based on the compensation measure originally used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for pay ratio disclosure filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay ratio information with respect to the registrant's last completed fiscal year is not required until the filing of its annual report on Form 10‑K for that fiscal year or, if later, the filing of a definitive proxy/information statement relating to its next annual meeting of shareholders; in any event must be filed no later than 120 days after the end of the fiscal year as provided in General Instruction G(3) of Form 10‑K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure pay ratio is included in the first required filing (Form 10‑K or later proxy) and adhere to the 120‑day filing backstop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and use of estimates for pay ratio calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may use reasonable estimates both in methodology to identify the median employee and in calculating annual total compensation or elements of compensation for employees other than the PEO. They may use employee population or statistical sampling and/or other reasonable methods, and may identify the median employee using annual total compensation or any other consistently applied compensation measure (e.g., tax or payroll records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a compensation measure recorded on a basis other than the registrant's fiscal year, registrant may use the same annual period used to derive those amounts. Where a compensation measure other than annual total compensation is used, disclose the measure used. Cost‑of‑living adjustments across jurisdictions are permitted to identify median employee but must be consistently applied and disclosed (including basis and jurisdiction). If cost‑of‑living adjustment used and median employee is outside PEO jurisdiction, also present median employee's annual total compensation and pay ratio without the adjustment. Briefly describe methodology and any material assumptions/estimates/adjustments; identify estimates used. If methodology or material assumptions changed from prior year and effects are significant, briefly describe change and reasons. Registrants may include personal benefits under $10,000 and compensation under non‑discriminatory benefit plans in median employee calculation if also included in PEO calculation; explain any material difference between PEO annual total compensation used in pay ratio and Summary Compensation Table amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted annualizing adjustments and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may annualize total compensation for permanent employees (full‑time or part‑time) employed less than the full fiscal year (e.g., newly hired employees or permanent employees on unpaid leave). A registrant may not annualize total compensation for temporary or seasonal positions and may not make a full‑time equivalent adjustment for any employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annualize only for permanent employees employed less than full year; do not annualize temps or use FTE conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEO compensation not available — disclosure and 8‑K filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If registrant is relying on Instruction 1 to Item 402(c)(2)(iii) and (iv) regarding the PEO's salary or bonus being undetermined, it shall disclose that the pay ratio is not calculable until the PEO salary or bonus is determined and disclose the date that the PEO's actual total compensation is expected to be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required pay ratio shall then be disclosed in the filing under Item 5.02(f) of Form 8‑K that discloses the PEO's salary or bonus when determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rules for registrants becoming subject to Item 402(u)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon becoming subject to Section 13(a) or 15(d) requirements, a registrant shall comply with paragraph (u) with respect to compensation for the first fiscal year following the year it became subject, but not for fiscal years commencing before January 1, 2017. Registrant may omit the disclosure until filing its Form 10‑K for that fiscal year or, if later, the proxy for the next annual meeting, but must file no later than 120 days after fiscal year end. A registrant may omit employees who became its employees as a result of a business combination/acquisition for the fiscal year in which the transaction becomes effective but must disclose approximate number omitted; include them in triennial calculations the following year. Registrant must comply with paragraph (u) for first fiscal year commencing on or after date it ceases to be a smaller reporting company (but not before Jan 1, 2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified transition and omission rules and disclose numbers and descriptions of omissions for acquired employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging growth company exemption for pay ratio disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant is not required to comply with paragraph (u) if it is an emerging growth company as defined in the Securities Act or Exchange Act. It shall comply with paragraph (u) for the first fiscal year commencing on or after the date it ceases to be an emerging growth company, but not for any fiscal year commencing before January 1, 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track emerging growth company status and commence disclosure in the first applicable fiscal year after status ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted supplemental pay ratio information limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may present additional information, including additional ratios, to supplement the required ratio, but are not required to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any additional information must be clearly identified, not misleading, and not presented with greater prominence than the required ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PEOs during the year — calculation options and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant with more than one non‑concurrent PEO during the fiscal year may calculate the PEO compensation either by: (1) calculating compensation provided to each person who served as PEO for the time served and combining those figures; or (2) looking to the PEO serving in the position on the date selected to identify the median employee and annualizing that PEO's compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of option selected, disclose which option was chosen and how the PEO's annual total compensation was calculated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees' personally identifiable information (PII) limitation in pay ratio disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are not required to, and should not, disclose any personally identifiable information about the median employee other than his or her compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may choose to generally identify an employee's position to put compensation in context, but should not do so if providing such information could identify any specific individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify applicable fiscal year in table titles for Item 402 tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the applicable fiscal year in the title to each table required under this Item which calls for disclosure as of or for a completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each table's title clearly indicates the fiscal year covered by the disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay versus performance disclosure — five‑year tabular requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the information specified for each of the registrant's last five completed fiscal years in the tabular format labeled "Pay Versus Performance" including columns for: Summary compensation table total for PEO; Compensation actually paid to PEO; Average summary compensation table total for non‑PEO named executive officers; Average compensation actually paid to non‑PEO named executive officers; Value of initial fixed $100 investment based on Net income, [Company‑selected measure], Total shareholder return, Peer group total shareholder return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the five‑year series in the required columns (a)–(i) and follow subsequent item (v)(2) rules for the specific elements to include and how to treat multiple PEOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay versus performance table — required elements for PEO and non‑PEO amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The table must include: (i) fiscal year (column (a)); (ii) PEO's total compensation for the covered fiscal year as reported in the Summary Compensation Table (column (b)), and average total compensation reported for remaining named executive officers (column (d)); (iii) executive compensation actually paid to the PEO (column (c)) and average executive compensation actually paid to the remaining named executive officers collectively (column (e)). If more than one person served as PEO during the covered fiscal year, provide separate columns for each such person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple PEOs served, provide separate columns for each such person for both reported total compensation and compensation actually paid, and follow the instructions for calculation and presentation.
